newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat after PPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat after PPI.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds opened unchanged as players took heart from an unexpected drop in October wholesale prices' core rate, despite a rise in the report overall.
"It was a good number, but I think a lot of it was built in," a municipal trader said.
Overall, the October Producer Price Index report showed a 0.4 percent rise versus expections for a gain of 0.2 percent, or, at most, 0.3 percent.
The core rate, which excludes the more volatile food and energy prices, fell 0.3 percent. Many economists had expected a 0.1 percent rise.
"The core was down (0.3 percent) so that more than balanced it off," a trader said.
Though the number was good, traders said municipal prices remained unchanged.

"A lot of the bids that were made yesterday are still there today. We haven't really made anything better," a trader said. "The market still feels pretty firm. I think the tone is still pretty solid."
A second trader said while the PPI number was favorable, the market had experienced a good run of late and remains "a little tired."
"I think it will probably grind around these levels for the day," he said.

Wednesday's actively quoted issues included Denver, Colo., City and County Airport 5-1/2 percent revenue refunding bonds of November 2013. The bonds, which are subject to the alternative minimum tax, had a net bid of 5.73 percent, versus a 5.74 percent net bid at Tuesday's close.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond lost some of its brief gains after PPI, but was up 4/32 at 100-28/32 to yield 6.43 percent. In debt futures, the December municipal contract was down 3/32 at 117-2/32. The December T-bond contract was flat at 114-29/32. The MOB spread was 69 ticks.
